requirements.goal: Game demo test and engine improvements: extend the game-core demo and, where gaps are found, the game-core engine itself, to cover game-engine capabilities not yet exercised. Scope is user-input-driven turn by turn rather than fully pre-planned.
requirements.constraints: Scope for each increment comes from the user's live direction turn by turn, not a pre-authored plan; each increment must still be a coherent, independently-mergeable slice with its own tests and, where a demo-visible change is involved, live verification via the .verify-scratch harness.
requirements.done: The user is satisfied that the demo and game-core module cover the game-engine capabilities they care about, and says so explicitly - there is no fixed feature checklist to complete.
requirements.outOfScope: No fully pre-planned feature list up front - increments are added one at a time as the user directs; no unrelated roadmap items (e.g. shutdown sequence, queue budget, web module) unless the user redirects to them explicitly.

increments.description: Fix phantom collision events - game-core's collision detection currently trusts rapier2d CollisionEvent::Started alone, but rapier2d 0.22 uses speculative/predictive contacts (IntegrationParameters::normalized_prediction_distance, default ~2mm scaled by length_unit): Started can fire for colliders that are merely within that margin, not actually touching, which is what produces the reported no-real-touch hit registrations. Fix: in publish_collisions, after draining a Started pair, confirm real geometric contact via physics.narrow_phase's ContactPair::has_any_active_contact before publishing a game-core/collision event; drop pairs that are speculative-only. Unit test: two colliders positioned within the prediction margin but not overlapping produce no collision event; two colliders that actually overlap still do.

Tune rapier2d solver stiffness against visible interpenetration - rapier2d's contact solver is compliant (spring-based TGS-soft) by design, not perfectly rigid; default IntegrationParameters (contact_natural_frequency, contact_damping_ratio, num_solver_iterations/num_internal_pgs_iterations) allow visible penetration under sustained driving force, which is what the reported overlapping-squares screenshots show. Raise contact stiffness (higher contact_natural_frequency, lower contact_damping_ratio if those fields exist on this exact 0.22.0 build, else the closest equivalent such as a consolidated contact_softness field) and solver iteration counts in Physics::new, and confirm the exact field names against the actual 0.22.0 API before editing (research pass gave educated-guess names that need compiler confirmation). Unit test: two bodies pushed together under continuous velocity settle to a measurably smaller steady-state penetration depth than before the change. Live-verify against the demo: push the robot into an obstacle and hold - overlap should be visibly reduced, though may not be fully eliminated (that is increment 3's job if this alone is insufficient).

Clamp commanded velocity against contact normals to stop overlap under sustained input - research confirms the primary mechanism behind visible interpenetration is set_velocity hard-overwriting rapier2d linear velocity every tick via body.set_linvel, which re-drives a body into an obstacle faster than the compliant solver's per-step corrective velocity (normalized_max_corrective_velocity) can push it back out, regardless of stiffness tuning (increment 2). Fix: before tick's physics.step, or immediately after via querying active contacts for each collider-bearing entity, zero or reflect the component of a Dynamic/Frictionless body's linear velocity that points into an active contact's normal (only when actually touching, i.e. has_any_active_contact, reusing increment 1's real-contact check) so continuous held input can push but not tunnel/overlap through a blocked direction while still allowing motion along the free axis (sliding along a wall). Unit test: a body driven continuously into a fixed obstacle settles at (or very near) zero penetration rather than the deeper steady-state overlap from before this increment, while a body driven diagonally against a wall still slides along the open axis. Live-verify: push the robot directly into a red obstacle and hold for several seconds - no visible overlap in a screenshot, and pushing diagonally still lets the robot slide along the obstacle's edge.
